interpretation_notes: What the read licenses: under the registration, a K1 v3 with a NEGATIVE region may be designed on Qwen3.5-4B-Base, with all seven requirements: D26's four (a seen-script condition, an entity-controlled set, the non-literal floor, a new id and the gauntlet) plus three from the flags (GO/NEGATIVE computed on the controlled set, anchor masking or a lexical-overlap covariate, H2 re-tested on the audit read). This is a pre-result about feasibility, measured on the development partition only (20 questions, 20 passage clusters, 7 held-out scripts, no seen-script pair). It still needs the program owner's decision.

What the read does not license: it says nothing about whether any indexer loses more cross-script recall than its target, either way. It is not a K1 GO or NEGATIVE. It does not cover the audit or primary partitions or seen-script pairs, and it does not show that Qwen3-0.6B can never support K1. It is development-partition headroom of a dense target over random at a matched 12.5% budget.

Compared with v1: v2's 0.6B lane is bit-identical to v1's job 727, so it adds no new information about 0.6B; it is only the validity anchor (NOT_VIABLE: H1_CX 12.25 with lower bound 8.98; H2 FAIL with H2b -3.93). The 4B lane is the only new measurement. There H1_CX is 42.15 (3.4x the 0.6B value) and Delta MN-CX is only 2.23 (0.44 to 3.87) against 8.55 on 0.6B. The 4B dense target attends to a cross-script needle almost as well as a same-script one, which leaves plenty of room for an indexer's loss to show.

Cross-lane comparison is confounded and should not be read as a model-scale effect. The 4B lane uses a different tokenizer: re-tokenized contexts up to 10,481 tokens, and non-English fertility of 1.25-3.0 against 1.54-6.41 for 0.6B. Recall averages over 8 of 32 full-attention layers there, against all 28. It ran a different attention kernel (memory-efficient, not cuDNN's) with warn-only determinism.

Fertility collinearity: on 4B, needle fertility correlates with CX headroom at -0.89 and with MN (same-language) headroom at exactly the same -0.89; on 0.6B the figures are -0.82 and -0.86. The association is therefore not cross-script-specific. It follows needle language (script and token length), and with seven languages it cannot be separated from script or unseen-language status. On 4B the query-side correlation is only -0.5, against -0.86 on 0.6B. Read STRONG as descriptive only.

The lexical confound is mostly not about entities. The literal selector's xi_rel is 0.265/0.274 on all families, 0.235/0.245 on controlled families and 0.30/0.31 on anchored ones. Content-token overlap between query and needle is about 0.46-0.54 on MN and about 0-0.03 on CX: it comes from same-language paraphrase in the MN leg, which is built into the MN-vs-CX contrast. So neither the entity-controlled set nor anchor masking will remove it. Only a lexical-overlap covariate, or a design that equalises overlap between legs, addresses it. A purely literal selector would read xi_rel of about 0.26, above K1's 0.10 limit, so any v3 GO signal is open to a lexical explanation unless that is handled.

The floor is permissive. The 99% lower bound of controlled G(MN) is at least 0.5 even for noisy copies far outside V1: at sigma 2.8, with an English ML loss of 26 points, the lower bound is still 0.518. The floor separates a literal-only selector (0.237) from target-like ones but does little beyond V1.

Robustness: lane_class is robust, with H1_CX lower bound 35.76 against 10 and point 42 against 20. The thinnest link in NEGATIVE_CAPABLE is H2b's point of 8.57 against 5, which is 24 net cells of 280 where 14 are needed. Its interval runs from -9.29 to 26.43, hence POINT_ONLY and the audit re-test requirement. The CENTRED and VIABLE flags rest on margins of 0.02-0.07 points (see problems); a flip would add requirements, not change the design.

Operation: the 4B lane ran 1,160 units in 479.5 s of evaluation and statistics against D44's estimates of 769-824 s, about 0.53/0.44/0.26/0.30 s per unit by stage. C-literal was the only stage slightly above its largest estimate (0.262 against 0.25). Used 9:17 of 32 minutes.
